styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: The Capitol, museums and live music history.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: BBQ, tacos and food trucks, all day.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Barton Springs, the Greenbelt and lake trails.

stays.why: Walk to the Capitol, Congress Avenue and Rainey Street. Best base for a first visit and nightlife.
Shops, cafés and food trucks on SoCo; a short ride or walk over the bridge to downtown.
Cheaper rooms near campus and the Blanton Museum; walkable and bus-friendly.
Galleries, bars and some of the city's best food; close to downtown but quieter.

food: Try Texas BBQ brisket and ribs. Popular spots have long lines; go early or expect a wait.
Breakfast tacos are a local staple. Cheap, filling and sold at many taquerias and trucks.
Food trucks cluster on South Congress and in East Austin. Cash is handy at some.
Book ahead for dinner on weekends, especially downtown and East Austin.
Tap water is safe to drink. Many places refill bottles; summers are hot, so carry water.
more_time: Add a day trip to the Hill Country: small towns and swimming holes west of the city. A car helps.
Swap an afternoon for a lake day on Lake Austin or Lady Bird Lake: kayak or paddleboard rentals.
Music fans can add a night of live shows on Sixth Street or Red River; check listings on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers BBQ, the Capitol and a Barton Springs swim. Add a night for live music and East Austin.

month_notes: Cool and quiet: highs near 16°C, lows near 6°C. Pack a warm layer.
Still cool, highs near 18°C. Good for walking; a few rainy days.
Mild and pleasant, highs near 23°C. Busy spring break weeks.
Warm, highs near 26°C. Great outdoor weather; more rain days.
Warm and wetter, highs near 29°C. Carry a rain jacket.
Hot, highs near 33°C. Plan outdoor time for morning.
Very hot, highs near 35°C. Stay hydrated and seek shade.
Hottest month, highs near 36°C. Do outdoor sights early.
Still hot, highs near 32°C. Pools and shade help.
Cooling down, highs near 28°C. Good festival season.
Mild, highs near 21°C. Comfortable for walking all day.
Cool, highs near 18°C. Light jacket for evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Subtropical: long hot summers, mild winters, and rain spread through the year.

items.title: Best time: March to May and October to November
items.text: Mild to warm days around 21–29°C. Ideal for walking, parks and patios.

items.title: Summer is very hot (June to September)
items.text: Highs of 32–36°C. Go outside early or after sunset and carry water.

items.title: Rain any month
items.text: About 8–16 rain days a month, most in May. Showers are often short.

items.title: Warm nights in summer
items.text: Lows stay near 22–25°C from June to September, so evenings stay hot.

items.title: Cool winter nights
items.text: December to February lows near 6–8°C. Bring a jacket for evenings.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes and sunscreen for summer; a light rain layer; a warm layer for winter nights.

transit.best: Ride apps or the bus for most trips; walk downtown and around UT.

modes.text: No metro or tram. A single commuter rail line (Red Line) runs north-south.
Capital Metro buses cover downtown, the Capitol and South Congress. Fares about $1.25 one way.
Uber and Lyft work well. Taxis exist but are less common.
Driving is common but traffic is heavy at rush hour; I-35 is often jammed.
Downtown and UT are walkable. Summers are very hot, so plan shade and water.
Bikes are popular and bike lanes exist on most major streets.
